To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the epigenetics of brain plasticity in response of stress are sex-dependent and that these epigenetic changes are associated with changes in gene expression that affect behavior, cognition, and physiology.

stress-induced changes in the adult brain are mediated by epigenetic mechanisms that alter the expression of genes involved in synaptic plasticity, neuronal survival, and neurogenesis, as well as by the regulation of steroid hormone receptors.
(1) the brain is the central integrator of information from the environment and the body and (2) the brain is a target of hormones, and hormones can alter brain development, function, and structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobiology of stress and the brain's role in mediating the stress response and the consequences for brain function and behavior.

understanding the molecular and neural mechanisms of stress-induced plasticity and the role of sex steroids in shaping the developing and adult brain, with an emphasis on the role of epigenetic processes.

the mechanisms by which environmental stressors, including social stressors such as maternal care and peer interactions, influence the development of the brain-body axis, and the consequences for health and disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain-body connection, mediated by the hypothalamus, has profound effects on the brain and body and that these effects are influenced by the sex of the individual.
we are just beginning to understand how the brain and body communicate, and we are only beginning to understand the role that sex and stress play in this process.

the brain is an integral part of the endocrine system, that the brain and body communicate with each other via hormonal and neural signals, and that the expression of steroid hormone receptor genes is critical to this bidirectional signaling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain is not only the central organ of the stress response but also the central organ of adaptation, and the brain-body connection has been the central theme of my research for over 30 years.
stress is a major determinant of brain and behavioral development, and that epigenetic processes mediate these effects.

the epigenetic landscape of stress is a dynamic process that begins before conception and continues throughout the life course, with the brain as the central organ of adaptation and the epigenome as the interface between the environment and the organism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is the central mediator of the effects of the environment on the body, and vice versa.

epigenetic changes in gene expression in the brain and body are induced by stress and can be passed from one generation to the next, and this is a critical component of the brain-body communication system.
stress and its consequences are not fixed and immutable but can be modified by the brain and the body.
